name: @buka/dsh-plugin-robots
description: Adds a Robots page to the sidebar that creates and manages its own robots: a robot is a directory under ~/.cache/dsh-plugin-robots/robots mounted as a DSH workspace, with project-level skills installed through npx skills, an editable AGENTS.md, and a one-click session. Every robot has a preset avatar (assigned on creation, changeable from the page), and the ctx.bukaRobots service exposes list(), avatarMap() and a robot session that can be continued by session id (its history is compacted before the next prompt); new robot sessions are normal conversations in the robot workspace and appear in the sidebar to other plugins. Installing the plugin also ships the robot-builder mode (an agent preset carried by its bundle patch): new sessions can pick 机器人构建, which interviews the user, drafts the robot's AGENTS.md, then creates and mounts the robot through the preset-gated buka_robot_build tool, while the page remains the manual path. A general-purpose robot is always listed first: fixed 🤖 avatar, standard mode, enters any existing workspace, and can be enabled or disabled from the page's Settings dialog (stored in settings.json next to robots.json). Every robot also has a one-sentence responsibility statement (like a skill description) that the buka_robots tool returns so a workflow orchestrator can decide whether to use that robot. While enabled, the general-purpose robot also appears at the end of the workflow robot list with the same fields as any other robot; disabling it removes it from that list.
